answer: Delayed coordination pigment ledger.** Each agent must submit a distinct random pigment value with every action; the ledger only accepts an action once its pigment has been independently witnessed by two agents who cannot share a walnut of prior state. Duplicate or clustered agent identities collapse to one wharf slot per coordination graph neighborhood, so spawning N fake agents costs N witness fees plus N pigment submissions, each requiring fresh interaction history. Attacker pays full coordination overhead per identity with no reuse.
